commits.subject: docs(plan): correct WS-C ordering and add funding cross-leg reconciliation design
commits.body:
Answers Codex's two review questions on
tasks/2026-08-03-project-optimization-codex-plan.md.

WS-C ordering: the previous order (C5 -> C3 -> C2 -> C6 -> C1 -> C7 -> C8) had
two dependency defects and is superseded by a four-phase order.
- C1 must follow C10. Feeding dd_tracker from get_equity() every ~2s while mids
  still come from raw WS delta levels wires a spiky equity into the hard-stop
  path, which can fire spurious hard stops or mask a real drawdown -- worse than
  today's fill-only updates.
- C2 must ship with the close_all repair. close_all is SWAP/cross-only inside a
  single try, so a hard stop wired to it would leave the dual-leg book's SPOT
  side open while appearing to flatten.
New order: Phase 1 inputs (C5, C10, C6, C11 Layer 1) -> Phase 2 venue-side
enforcement (C3, close_all) -> Phase 3 guards (C7, C1, C2, C8) -> Phase 4
accounting (C4, C9, C11 Layers 2-3).

Funding cross-leg reconciliation: documents a prerequisite defect found while
answering -- portfolio_manager.py:314 passes the perp mid as `preferred` to
_resolve_price, and _resolve_price returns `preferred` when positive, so the
spot leg is priced off the perp book whenever the perp mid exists. In contango
that makes a spot buy cross the spot spread, so post_only rejects the hedge leg
while the primary leg is already filled -- one concrete cause of naked exposure.
Adds the four-layer design (pre-flight validation, leg group identity, post-fill
reconciliation that unwinds rather than chases, journal/alert/gate metric) with
binary acceptance criteria.

All 21 cited anchors re-verified against 6bdafa0; stale line numbers from before
the paper-demo batch (1992ac2) corrected, and the parts that batch already fixed
are listed so they are not redone.

commits.author: Frisk0316
commits.subject: fix(artifacts): route DATABASE_URL through cfg so local backtest scripts write to DB
commits.body:
Previously, _artifact_mode() and the two upsert helpers read DATABASE_URL
directly from os.environ. run_replay_backtest.py calls load_config with
require_secrets=False, which skips .env loading entirely, so os.environ
never had DATABASE_URL and artifact_mode always fell back to "files".

Changes:
- config.py: bridge DATABASE_URL env var into storage.timescale_dsn when
  load_config() builds StorageConfig and YAML omits timescale_dsn. All
  callers that pass cfg now get the DSN without touching os.environ.
- artifacts.py: _artifact_mode(dsn) accepts explicit dsn parameter instead
  of reading os.environ directly (os.environ remains as fallback).
- _upsert_run_to_db and _upsert_artifacts_to_db accept dsn and mode params
  instead of each re-reading os.environ independently.
- save_backtest_artifacts resolves dsn from cfg.storage.timescale_dsn once
  and passes it through to all helpers.

Result: python scripts/run_replay_backtest.py now writes to DB when
DATABASE_URL is set, without needing load_dotenv() or manual env exports.
